items.title: Joe Darensbourg and Minor "Ram" Hall Interview, 1957-04-18
items.q: started working for these gangsters, Charlie Berger and his gang.

ctx.x: Joe Poston? Yeah. Just playing with Jimmy New York? He was playing saxophone. Yeah? Yeah.

And Zooty, Zooty had been around St. Louis just before then. It was really in Chicago last time. Well, Zooty had been playing in St. Louis though, I hadn't been playing with those guys, but they was talking about him. Then I played around there for a long, uh, not, well, not too long. Then I went to, uh, Harrisburg, Illinois with, with a bunch of guys and started working for these gangsters, Charlie Berger and his gang.
Yeah. Well, I'll tell them, tell us about St. Louis.

items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: So I told Charlie Berger, this gangster, "I'd like to stay here and work."

ctx.x: Let me just get back to the factual side of things. Chronologically almost, we've got you to the point whereby you said you went to St. Louis. You left the medicine show in St. Louis?

No. Not at first. When I got through in St. Louis, we went up, played up through Illinois and parts of Ohio. And we wound up in Harrisburg, Illinois. We was playing in Harrisburg, which at that time was called Bloody Williamson County, where they had bunches of syndicate... They had a bunch of roadhouses in those days and bootlegging joints. We played Harrisburg, and we got off the medicine show, and they had a place called Shady Rest. The (?) said they had a good band out there, where you could go jam. They had…
